_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL, NOS) or large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) arising from follicular lymphoma, after two or more lines of systemic therapy

pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory DLBCL, NOS or transformed follicular lymphoma after at least two prior systemic therapies; median age 67, median 3 prior lines, 30% had prior CAR-T cell therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Prespecified primary endpoint was IRC-assessed complete response (CR) rate per Lugano 2014 criteria
pivotal_trials.result: IRC-assessed ORR 56% (95% CI: 47, 65) with CR rate 43% (95% CI: 35, 52); estimated median DOR 18.4 months (95% CI: 11.4, NE) and 9-month DOR rate 68.5% (95% CI: 56.7, 80.3) at median follow-up 11.6 months

key_safety: Adverse reactions occurred in 99% of patients (Grade 3+ in 64%); serious ARs 48%, fatal ARs 5%. Most common non-laboratory ARs (>=20%) were CRS (70%, including Grade 2 in 14%, Grade 3 in 2.8%, Grade 4 in 1.4%), musculoskeletal pain (21%), fatigue (20%), and rash (20%); ICANS reported in 4.8%
target_moa: Bispecific CD20-directed CD3 T-cell engager; binds CD20 on B cells and CD3 on T cells, causing T-cell activation and proliferation, cytokine secretion, and lysis of CD20-expressing B cells

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), including serious or fatal reactions; premedicate and use step-up dosing to reduce risk

rems.type: FDA concurred that additional REMS are not required for the safe use of glofitamab in the indicated population

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) with durability of response (DOR), intermediate/surrogate endpoints in the single-arm trial

citations.quote: However, when interpreting the results, it is important to note that the efficacy of the study drug was based on ORR, CR and DoR, which are intermediate endpoints evaluated in a single arm trial.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Required randomized confirmatory trial comparing glofitamab + GemOx to rituximab + GemOx in R/R DLBCL, with overall survival as primary endpoint

citations.quote: 4464-1 Complete a randomized clinical trial that evaluates the clinical benefit of glofitamab in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The trial should compare glofitamab in combination with gemcitabine and oxaliplatin (GemOx) to rituximab in combination with GemOx for patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The primary endpoint should be overall survival with secondary endpoints that include progression-free survival and response rate.

summary.text: Glofitamab-gxbm received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 601.41 based on ORR/CR rate with durability (intermediate endpoints) from the single-arm Study NP30179, with a Priority review, and a required randomized confirmatory trial to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: It is approved under accelerated approval pursuant to section 506(c) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) and 21 CFR 601.41, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon approved labeling.
However, when interpreting the results, it is important to note that the efficacy of the study drug was based on ORR, CR and DoR, which are intermediate endpoints evaluated in a single arm trial.
Pursuant to section 506(c) of the FDCA and 21 CFR 601.41, you are required to conduct further adequate and well-controlled clinical trial intended to verify and describe clinical benefit.

requirement.text: 4464-1: Complete a randomized clinical trial evaluating the clinical benefit of glofitamab in DLBCL, comparing glofitamab + GemOx to rituximab + GemOx, with overall survival as the primary endpoint (accelerated approval confirmatory trial)

citations.quote: 4464-1 Complete a randomized clinical trial that evaluates the clinical benefit of glofitamab in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The trial should compare glofitamab in combination with gemcitabine and oxaliplatin (GemOx) to rituximab in combination with GemOx for patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The primary endpoint should be overall survival with secondary endpoints that include progression-free survival and response rate.

requirement.text: 4464-2: Conduct a study assessing efficacy and safety of glofitamab in pediatric patients 6 months or older with relapsed or refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma (deferred pediatric study under PREA)

citations.quote: 4464-2 Conduct a study assessing the efficacy and safety of glofitamab in pediatric patients 6 months or older with relapsed or refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The safety endpoints should evaluate safety and tolerability of glofitamab monotherapy and in combination with standard chemotherapy and identify the recommended dosage. The efficacy endpoints should evaluate activity as assessed by response rate and durability of response.

requirement.text: 4464-3: Conduct an integrated analysis of clinical trial data to further characterize safety, efficacy, PK, and pharmacodynamics of glofitamab among U.S. racial and ethnic minority patients with large B-cell lymphoma

citations.quote: 4464-3 Conduct an integrated analysis of data from clinical trials to further characterize the safety, efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of glofitamab among U.S. racial and ethnic minority patients with large B-cell lymphoma. The population should be representative of the U.S. population of patients with large B-cell lymphoma, including racial and ethnic diversity, and allow for interpretation of the results in these populations.

requirement.text: 4464-4: Conduct an analysis of duration of response with extended follow-up in patients who discontinue glofitamab monotherapy after receiving 12 cycles, in the primary efficacy population of Study NP30179

citations.quote: 4464-4 Conduct an analysis of duration of response with extended follow-up in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma or transformed follicular lymphoma who discontinue glofitamab monotherapy after receiving 12 cycles. Provide this additional duration of response data, as assessed by an IRC, in patients in the primary efficacy population of Study NP30179, with a targeted minimum of one year of extended follow-up after completion of 12 cycles of glofitamab. Include data regarding new anti-lymphoma therapy and efficacy outcomes after glofitamab retreatment.
